outcome: On 21 September 2026 Matthew J. Colbrook (Cambridge) posted a preprint, on Zenodo and with a Lean 4 formalisation on GitHub, showing that the unrestricted statement fails: for each c > 4 an explicit polynomial ODE on R^5 with uniformly negative divergence has a compact global attractor whose local Lyapunov dimension is 4+4/c, attained on an invariant two-torus with an irrational linear flow, while equilibria and periodic orbits reach at most 3. The author's own declaration says a Codex agent was used to obtain the counterexample. No public human engagement was found in the 19 days since posting, and the registry entry the repository cites could not be confirmed.
problem_asks: The bullet asks one universal claim with three parts. (a) For a dynamical system with a global attractor, the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions taken over that attractor is achieved. (b) The supremum is achieved at a stationary point (equilibrium) lying in the attractor. (c) Alternatively, the supremum is achieved on an unstable periodic orbit embedded into the attractor. The bullet carries no restriction on the class of systems or attractors, so as worded it is the unrestricted statement. Read as written, it asserts the conclusion for every system with a global attractor. Eden's 1987 proposal and the restricted or refined versions discussed in the literature (Kuznetsov's self-excited and hidden attractor versions) are not named in the bullet.

events.what_happened: Matthew J. Colbrook (University of Cambridge, DAMTP) posted 'Aperiodic maximisers of Lyapunov dimension: A counterexample to the unrestricted form of Eden's conjecture' on Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22883032, version v1 only, resource type preprint, CC BY 4.0, 'Created and modified September 21, 2026'. The Zenodo abstract, as relayed to me, says it disproves the unrestricted form, which holds that the maximal local Lyapunov dimension on a compact global attractor is attained at an equilibrium or periodic orbit. For each c > 4 it constructs a polynomial differential equation on R^5 with uniformly negative divergence whose attractor has Lyapunov dimension 4+4/c, attained precisely on an invariant two-torus carrying an irrational linear flow, while the maximum over equilibria and periodic orbits is 3. The repository's PALOMAR.md says it holds for the local dimension defined by singular values at every positive time and for the asymptotic Kaplan-Yorke dimension, and that the attractor is nontransitive, with no claim for transitive, strange or typical attractors. The PDF itself could not be read with my tools (see incomplete), so the theorem statement is taken from the abstract and repository files, not from the paper's text.
events.revisions: v1 only on Zenodo, 'Versions' section empty as of 10 Oct 2026. Repository has six commits from 21 to 22 Sep 2026; the first, d847493 (2026-09-21 23:13:04 UTC), adds the Lean formalisation (see colbrook-2026-lean-repo).
events.delivers: For every c > 4, an explicit polynomial vector field on R^5 with uniformly negative divergence and a compact global attractor on which the maximal local Lyapunov dimension is 4+4/c, reached only on an invariant two-torus with an irrational linear flow. Since the maximum over equilibria and periodic orbits in that attractor is 3, the supremum is attained neither at an equilibrium nor at a periodic orbit for this family, which contradicts the bullet's claim for these systems. Restrictions the paper states: it concerns the unrestricted conjecture only; the attractor is nontransitive; the claim covers the local dimension defined by singular values at every positive time and the asymptotic Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Dimension 5 and the single explicit family for each c > 4 are the whole scope.
events.remains: Part (a) is settled for this family only, and parts (b) and (c) are shown to fail for it. Not addressed: whether the statement holds for transitive, strange or typical attractors (expressly not claimed); the self-excited and hidden attractor refinements that Kuznetsov proposed; whether counterexamples exist in other dimensions or other classes of systems; and whether the specific systems Wikipedia lists as verified (Lorenz, complex Ginzburg-Landau, self-excited Lorenz, Henon map) are affected, which the paper does not discuss as far as I could tell.

events.directly_checkable: The vector field family is explicit. The repository's READING_GUIDE describes a five-dimensional ambient space with parameter c > 4 and a fifth component -c*w, so the uniform negative divergence can be checked by hand from the field. The dimension values 4+4/c and 3 need the paper's argument. The Lean statement is named EdenPalomar.main_theorem in PalomarChallenge.lean.
events.doubts: (1) Single author, a Zenodo preprint without a journal or referee report found; the author's publications page could not be opened, so I cannot confirm its status. (2) The construction and the counterexample were obtained with an AI agent (Codex, per the author's declaration), and the author says he checked them; no independent human reading is publicly recorded. (3) The Lean statements in PalomarChallenge.lean and Challenge.lean were prepared with AI assistance and checked against Theorem 1.1 by Codex, so whether the formal statement matches the paper's definitions rests on the author's and the agent's check; the Palomar statement says the registry does not certify this. (4) The repository states both that the Palomar registration is final and that a passing report is required before submission, and I could not see the entry, so the registry status is unresolved. (5) Dimension values come from the abstract as relayed; the paper's own derivation was not read.
events.direction: Against the bullet. The bullet says the supremum is attained at an equilibrium or an unstable periodic orbit. For this family the supremum is attained on an invariant torus, and no equilibrium or periodic orbit reaches it (3 against 4+4/c). The bullet is unrestricted, so the plain reading is that this cuts against it for these systems. Whether it cuts against the refined versions the literature actually tests is not decided by this event.
events.object: An explicit family, one polynomial vector field on R^5 for each c > 4, with uniformly negative divergence and a compact global attractor. On the attractor's invariant two-torus, which carries an irrational linear flow, the local Lyapunov dimension is 4+4/c, and this is the maximum. Equilibria and periodic orbits in the attractor give at most 3. The object is explicit, not from a non-constructive existence argument, per the repository's formalization.yaml ('an explicit polynomial ODE on Euclidean five-space'). The exact vector field was not read from the paper.

events.what_happened: Daniel Kressner (EPFL) and Bart Vandereycken (University of Geneva), arXiv:2608.20875 [math.NA], 'A counterexample to the symmetric-maximizer conjecture for Lyapunov operators', stamped 21 Aug 2026. It gives an integer matrix of order 7 whose skew-symmetric restricted norm of the Frobenius-induced Lyapunov operator exceeds its symmetric restricted norm, with exact rational certificates, and a direct-sum extension to n >= 7. It is discounted here: it concerns operator norms of Lyapunov operators, not Lyapunov dimension or Eden's conjecture, and it does not cite Colbrook's preprint.

events.delivers: Settles a different conjecture: that the operator norm of the Lyapunov operator is attained at a symmetric matrix, now refuted for orders 7 and above, with order 6 open. Nothing about attractors, Lyapunov dimension or unstable periodic orbits.
events.remains: All parts of the Eden bullet. This event does not bear on it.

events.what_happened: N. V. Kuznetsov and T. N. Mokaev, 'A note on finite-time Lyapunov dimension of the Rossler attractor', arXiv:1807.00235, submitted 30 June 2018. Abstract: 'For the Rossler system we verify Eden's conjecture on the maximum of local Lyapunov dimension.' The verification is numerical: finite-time local Lyapunov dimensions on the Rossler attractor and on embedded unstable periodic orbits, with the orbits found by Pyragas time-delay feedback control.
events.delivers: For the Rossler system alone, a numerical check of the maximum of local Lyapunov dimension against embedded unstable periodic orbits. It is a finite-time computation for one system, not a proof, and it does not address the general statement.
events.remains: The general statement for all systems with global attractors. Also the Rossler dimension itself, which Leonov conjectured equals a stationary point's local dimension; the paper does not settle it.
events.directly_checkable: The numerical method is described in the abstract, but I did not read the full paper.
events.doubts: A finite-time numerical computation of local Lyapunov dimension is not a proof. The later Lorenz paper by the same group (arXiv:1910.08740) says reliable numerical computation of finite-time Lyapunov dimension over long trajectories is itself a difficulty.
events.direction: Consistent with the bullet for the Rossler system, as far as a finite-time numerical check can show. Not a counterexample.

It proves the exact Lyapunov dimension formula for the Lorenz global attractor over a wider parameter range, including all parameters satisfying the classical physical limitations. The abstract does not mention Eden's conjecture or a maximum at the zero equilibrium. Wikipedia cites 'Leonov et al., 2016' for the Lorenz case; I have not confirmed that this arXiv preprint is that citation.

summary: I found one event that bears on the bullet as worded: Matthew J. Colbrook's Zenodo preprint of 21 September 2026, 'Aperiodic maximisers of Lyapunov dimension: A counterexample to the unrestricted form of Eden's conjecture' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22883032). It is a single-author, unrefereed preprint with a Lean 4 formalisation on GitHub. The Zenodo landing page and the repository files, which Colbrook maintains, describe the result: for each c > 4 an explicit polynomial ODE on R^5 with uniformly negative divergence and a compact global attractor whose local Lyapunov dimension is 4+4/c, reached only on an invariant two-torus with an irrational linear flow, while equilibria and periodic orbits reach at most 3. The bullet, which is unrestricted, would require the supremum to be attained at an equilibrium or a periodic orbit. So for this family the result cuts against the bullet. I could not read the PDF with my tools, so the theorem statement and the AI declaration are taken from the repository's formalization.yaml and PALOMAR.md, which quote the paper's page-9 declaration and reach me through a summarising fetch. The quotes are therefore not verbatim-checked against the PDF. The author's declaration, as relayed, says ChatGPT 6 was used in discussions and in Lean verification, and that Codex (an agent harness, with ChatGPT 6 as its listed model) was used first to attempt a proof and then to obtain the counterexample. The repository says the author checked the proof and formulation against the paper and adopted its contents. Two systems are therefore credited: Codex with obtaining the counterexample, which is load-bearing on the author's account, and ChatGPT 6 with discussions and Lean assistance, whose role in the mathematics the repository does not state. No independent human reading or public engagement turned up in my searches, which covered Mathstodon, Tao, news, the Palomar registry and the literature; the search engine indexes blogs and social media poorly, so silence here is weak evidence. The Palomar registry entry the repository cites (PALOMAR-2026-09-22-000001) could not be confirmed: the registry's data feed, read from 23 Sep to 10 Oct 2026, has no entry dated 22 September. Before 2024 the conjecture had been verified only for specific systems: Kuznetsov and Mokaev's 2018 numerical check for the Rossler system (arXiv 1807.00235); the 2019 Lorenz verification report (arXiv 1910.08740; I found no March 2024 revision, despite an earlier search snippet saying so); the exact Lorenz dimension formula (arXiv 1508.07498); and, per Wikipedia only, the Doering et al. 1987 Ginzburg-Landau result, the Leonov-Lyashko 1993 Lorenz result, and the Kuznetsov self-excited Henon results of 2017 and 2021. These are instances, not the general statement. The Wikipedia article was last edited on 2 September 2026, before the preprint, so its silence on the counterexample is not informative. Kressner and Vandereycken's arXiv 2608.20875 (21 Aug 2026), which credits gpt-5.6-sol, concerns a different conjecture (symmetric maximisers for Lyapunov operators) and is recorded only as a discounted neighbour. Close calls: (1) Whether the counterexample refutes the bullet depends on whether the bullet is read as the unrestricted statement, which its wording suggests, or as the conjecture in the literature sense (verified for particular systems and refined by Kuznetsov for self-excited and hidden attractors), which the counterexample does not address. The paper's own title ('unrestricted form') treats the two as distinct. (2) Whether the AI was load-bearing: the author says Codex 'obtain[ed] the counterexample', which is load-bearing on the author's account, but the repository gives no detail on how, and I could not read the paper's own account.
competing_reading: The bullet names no restriction, so the plain reading is the unrestricted statement, and this counterexample refutes it outright for every c > 4 in R^5. The competing reading is that Eden's conjecture, as the literature uses the name, is the claim verified for well-known systems (Lorenz, complex Ginzburg-Landau, self-excited Lorenz, Henon) and refined by Kuznetsov for self-excited and hidden attractors. On that reading the counterexample is to a stronger claim than the one the field is testing, and the bullet is not contradicted for the cases it names. The paper's own title ('unrestricted form') supports the view that a restricted form is a separate question.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The paper's PDF, read directly: the theorem statement, definitions of the local and Kaplan-Yorke dimensions, and the page-9 AI declaration verbatim, to replace the relayed quotes. (2) The Palomar registry entry for PALOMAR-2026-09-22-000001 or a confirmed absence of it, from the registry's own entry page or API. (3) A public verification or refutation by a dynamical-systems specialist, such as Kuznetsov's group, Leonov, Boichenko, or Colbrook's peers, or a journal referee report. (4) Journal publication or rejection of the preprint. (5) Independent confirmation that the Lean statements in Challenge.lean match Theorem 1.1, and whether the restricted and self-excited versions are addressed by any later work.

event.what_happened: Matthew J. Colbrook (University of Cambridge, DAMTP) posted 'Aperiodic maximisers of Lyapunov dimension: A counterexample to the unrestricted form of Eden's conjecture' on Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22883032, version v1 only, resource type preprint, CC BY 4.0, 'Created and modified September 21, 2026'. The Zenodo abstract, as relayed to me, says it disproves the unrestricted form, which holds that the maximal local Lyapunov dimension on a compact global attractor is attained at an equilibrium or periodic orbit. For each c > 4 it constructs a polynomial differential equation on R^5 with uniformly negative divergence whose attractor has Lyapunov dimension 4+4/c, attained precisely on an invariant two-torus carrying an irrational linear flow, while the maximum over equilibria and periodic orbits is 3. The repository's PALOMAR.md says it holds for the local dimension defined by singular values at every positive time and for the asymptotic Kaplan-Yorke dimension, and that the attractor is nontransitive, with no claim for transitive, strange or typical attractors. The PDF itself could not be read with my tools (see incomplete), so the theorem statement is taken from the abstract and repository files, not from the paper's text.
event.revisions: v1 only on Zenodo, 'Versions' section empty as of 10 Oct 2026. Repository has six commits from 21 to 22 Sep 2026; the first, d847493 (2026-09-21 23:13:04 UTC), adds the Lean formalisation (see colbrook-2026-lean-repo).
event.delivers: For every c > 4, an explicit polynomial vector field on R^5 with uniformly negative divergence and a compact global attractor on which the maximal local Lyapunov dimension is 4+4/c, reached only on an invariant two-torus with an irrational linear flow. Since the maximum over equilibria and periodic orbits in that attractor is 3, the supremum is attained neither at an equilibrium nor at a periodic orbit for this family, which contradicts the bullet's claim for these systems. Restrictions the paper states: it concerns the unrestricted conjecture only; the attractor is nontransitive; the claim covers the local dimension defined by singular values at every positive time and the asymptotic Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Dimension 5 and the single explicit family for each c > 4 are the whole scope.
event.remains: Part (a) is settled for this family only, and parts (b) and (c) are shown to fail for it. Not addressed: whether the statement holds for transitive, strange or typical attractors (expressly not claimed); the self-excited and hidden attractor refinements that Kuznetsov proposed; whether counterexamples exist in other dimensions or other classes of systems; and whether the specific systems Wikipedia lists as verified (Lorenz, complex Ginzburg-Landau, self-excited Lorenz, Henon map) are affected, which the paper does not discuss as far as I could tell.

event.directly_checkable: The vector field family is explicit. The repository's READING_GUIDE describes a five-dimensional ambient space with parameter c > 4 and a fifth component -c*w, so the uniform negative divergence can be checked by hand from the field. The dimension values 4+4/c and 3 need the paper's argument. The Lean statement is named EdenPalomar.main_theorem in PalomarChallenge.lean.
event.doubts: (1) Single author, a Zenodo preprint without a journal or referee report found; the author's publications page could not be opened, so I cannot confirm its status. (2) The construction and the counterexample were obtained with an AI agent (Codex, per the author's declaration), and the author says he checked them; no independent human reading is publicly recorded. (3) The Lean statements in PalomarChallenge.lean and Challenge.lean were prepared with AI assistance and checked against Theorem 1.1 by Codex, so whether the formal statement matches the paper's definitions rests on the author's and the agent's check; the Palomar statement says the registry does not certify this. (4) The repository states both that the Palomar registration is final and that a passing report is required before submission, and I could not see the entry, so the registry status is unresolved. (5) Dimension values come from the abstract as relayed; the paper's own derivation was not read.
event.direction: Against the bullet. The bullet says the supremum is attained at an equilibrium or an unstable periodic orbit. For this family the supremum is attained on an invariant torus, and no equilibrium or periodic orbit reaches it (3 against 4+4/c). The bullet is unrestricted, so the plain reading is that this cuts against it for these systems. Whether it cuts against the refined versions the literature actually tests is not decided by this event.
event.object: An explicit family, one polynomial vector field on R^5 for each c > 4, with uniformly negative divergence and a compact global attractor. On the attractor's invariant two-torus, which carries an irrational linear flow, the local Lyapunov dimension is 4+4/c, and this is the maximum. Equilibria and periodic orbits in the attractor give at most 3. The object is explicit, not from a non-constructive existence argument, per the repository's formalization.yaml ('an explicit polynomial ODE on Euclidean five-space'). The exact vector field was not read from the paper.

judgement.why: The statement is a universal, unrestricted claim that the supremum of local Lyapunov dimension over a global attractor is attained at an equilibrium or periodic orbit. A single explicit system whose maximum sits only on an invariant torus (4+4/c against at most 3) contradicts it, so Colbrook's preprint answers the whole question in the negative: scope whole, direction refuted, object a counterexample. It is unreviewed: the only human check is the author's own, and the Lean build is not digestion (F7). The dimension values also need the paper's argument, so it is not 'checkable'. It is credible: the author is an established researcher, the formalisation is substantial and no specific error has been identified; 19 days of silence is not a reason for doubt. The AI role is generated, because the author's declaration says Codex was used 'to obtain the counterexample'. ChatGPT 6's quoted role (discussions, Lean assistance) is thin and earns nothing on its own. The Lean repository formalises the same argument and adds no mathematics, so its scope is none and, being formalisation work, its AI role is none. Kressner–Vandereycken is a different conjecture (variant). The pre-2024 single-system verifications are instances, and the Hénon self-excited results address Kuznetsov's refinement (variant).
judgement.doubts: The close call is the competing reading: whether Eden's conjecture means the unrestricted statement or the literature's restricted or self-excited forms. I answered on the bullet's wording, which is unrestricted; the paper's own title concedes that a restricted form remains open. The AI quote and the theorem statement reach the record through repository files and a summarising fetch, not the PDF itself, so they are not verbatim-checked. The Palomar registry entry is unconfirmed. Verification for the pre-snapshot journal papers is assumed from journal publication as cited by Wikipedia; it does not affect the outcome.
